Hi Elena / Marissa — answering the core items from the SSQ inline at a high level, and attaching a brief subprocessor attestation PDF. I'll follow up with more granular artifacts if you need them.

1) PII handling & classification- We mark HealthStream data as "sensitive customer PII" when ingested per contract. Classification mapping: identifier (patient_id, ssn) = Sensitive; demographic fields (age, city) = Restricted. We redact or tokenize on request; by default Redwood does not perform de-identification unless configured by the customer.

2) Data flow and caching- Runtime flow: inbound request -> frontend validation -> routing -> model inference nodes. Transient KV cache stores session tokens/encodings for latency optimization (TTL configurable). Persistent logs (request metadata, billing tokens) are stored in encrypted object storage. See attached RS_DataFlow_v1.svg for component boundaries.

3) Subprocessors- Current list (as of 2027-05-21):
  - CloudComputeCo (gpu-rendering, us-east-1) — subprocessors/cloudcomputeco
  - MetricsHouse (analytics, us-west-2) — metricshouse.example.com
  - LogStore Inc. (audit log persistence, eu-west-1) — we use LogStore only for customers that opt into extended retention
  - KeyCustody Ltd. (KMS/HSM provider) — supports HSM-backed keys; we integrate with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys via envelope encryption

We maintain subprocessor contracts and perform due diligence; attestation included [Attachment: Subprocessor_Attestation_20270521.pdf].

4) Cross-border transfer mechanisms- For EU personal data we support Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and rely on adequacy where available. For private deployments we can restrict processing to region-specific clusters (VPC/private deployment).

5) Key management- Customer-managed keys are supported in Dedicated and Private modes; hosted customers may use Redwood-managed KMS unless a dedicated key is requested (additional onboarding). Keys are HSM-backed when using KeyCustody Ltd.

6) Retention & exportability- Retention is configurable by route. Audit logs and request logs can be exported on-demand; we provide a playspace for legal/forensics exports and can supply manifests.

7) Model training- Redwood does not train or fine-tune public models on customer prompt data for hosted customers by default. Any training activity is an explicit cadence and must be contracted.

Next steps:
- We'll complete the SSQ and send the redline-ready DPA annex.
- Marissa — if HealthStream needs SCC language in the draft DPA annex, flag it now and we'll include the transfer exhibit.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Subprocessor_Attestation_20270521.pdf]
